user_linear_extrapolation.supported_conclusion: A blind plan to send 500M new full-schema requests at this benchmark workload is expensive and this exact serial worker is slow. This arithmetic is not a qualified full-corpus delivery quote or proof that parallel acceleration is impossible.

quota_interpretation_limits: The actual-token scenarios assume all stated TPM can continuously serve the same mean input+output workload with enough concurrency and no bottlenecks. They are optimistic fluid arithmetic, not measured Azure throughput.
Azure rate admission can account estimated input and maximum requested completion tokens rather than billed token totals; actual billing-token means alone do not predict admission rate.
The unchanged-worker reservation rows ignore 60-second bin packing, request latency, validation, I/O and other shared traffic; parallel requests cannot evade the shared token budget.
250k was total model quota at preflight, not 250k extra on top of the 100k deployment. No quota changes were made in this audit.
300k existing Kimi capacity cannot simply be borrowed by Luna. A hypothetical 300k Luna row is not authorization or proof of available quota.
Parallelism can improve wall time until a token/requests/service/IO bottleneck binds. It does not by itself reduce billed tokens or dollars.
All rows assume the unrepresentative fixed20 workload, with no quality-approved large-corpus distribution or saturation benchmark.

scope_correction.selection_bias: First20 eligible known-full/no-unknown candidates from 68 eligible among a frozen200 audit frame; 106unknown/unresolved,22prior exceptions/noncandidates,4protected were excluded.
required_accounting: Verify corpus unit: source rows, canonical ads and complete-input contexts are different denominators. Preserve requested full scope.
Union historical results by verified complete-input identity and compatible frozen schema/field version, not by filename or adding counts.
Reuse accepted field results and retained compatible rule/coarse features without claiming their engineering acceptance proves missing fine semantics.
For duplicate contexts, reuse only verified exact compatible full inputs and preserve all ad mappings; no assumed global dedup fraction or fuzzy semantic equivalence.
Preserve reviewed_unknown/partial and protected states distinctly. Unknown does not automatically become an unprocessed model task; provider-quarantined content is not rerouted or retried.
New semantic request count must come from verified missing, eligible context/field work, plus separately bounded AI checks. Saved_unverified is not accepted and does not authorize blind rerun.
scope_correction.simplified_forward_budget_formula: new_eligible_requests * matched_mean_request_cost + separately_bounded_QA_and_rework + compute/storage/network; current benchmark mean is only a planning sensitivity until workload/quality are qualified
scope_correction.primary_estimation_scope: New verified eligible unprocessed contexts U_new only; 500M all-new-call arithmetic retained solely to audit the users extrapolation and reject blind full rerun.

5000_usd_caution.interpretation: At this measured per-call workload, $5000 buys only ~6.047M call-equivalents before infrastructure and QA. Finishing full coverage under that amount would require proven reuse/cheaper qualified processing for the rest; it is not established.

decision_supported: Use the user-reported1M TPM ceiling at80–90% shared-budget assumption for conditional new-work planning; keep effective same-model quota unverified until read-only confirmation, and do not upgrade configuration in this audit.
Do not expand the 20-record Luna benchmark into 500M blind new requests. No production expansion is launched by this audit.
Inventory and reuse existing framework/results first; determine real missing semantic work rather than substituting500M rows with500M API requests.
Keep Luna outputs as compatibility-test sidecars. 14/20 engineering pass and2/14 literal structure matches do not establish semantic accuracy or certify production quality.

If future runtime optimization is authorized, add explicit per-stage timing and bounded saturation tests before quoting finish dates; do not alter frozen research schema to make the price look better.

primary_planning_scenario.planning_unit: unique eligible complete-input context requiring a new semantic call; not every source row or saved output
limits: 1M is a user-reported planning ceiling only; same-model deployment quota, service admission accounting, requests/minute and all shared consumers must be verified before use.
Using 80–90% shared budget does not override the existing100k Luna worker cap; this audit makes no changes.
The observed20 records were QA rereads of already-saved candidates, not20 new corpus coverage increments. The remaining U_new must come from a nonduplicative asset/field/context ledger.
5131.75 tokens and$0.000826815 are the biased20-record workload means, not a certified global distribution. 80–90% headroom is a planning assumption, not measured efficiency.

Optimistic billed-token arithmetic is not an attainable-throughput promise. The current byte-upper-bound plus12000-output reservation is7.0493 times observed billed tokens, and service rate admission may also reserve maximum output.
Concurrency can help fill legitimate capacity but cannot bypass shared token limits or cure the benchmark quality failures. No claim of finishing the project for$5000 is made.
